classification.difficultyReason: Explain why a schematic graph cannot represent the equation by checking the origin.

content.prompt:
Ed has drawn the line with equation $y = -x$.
Explain how you know that Ed must have made a mistake.

spec.description: Unticked, unscaled axes and a descending blue segment crossing the vertical axis above the origin. Internal drawing coordinates specify schematic placement only and introduce no numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Negative slope; positive vertical intercept; entire supplied segment above the horizontal axis; line does not pass through the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: The intentionally incorrect line remains visible; no corrected line is supplied.

answer.short: It must pass through the origin because $(0,0)$ satisfies $y = -x$.
answer.worked:
At $(0,0)$:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{LHS} &= 0\\\text{RHS} &= -(0)\\&= 0\end{aligned}$$
LHS $=$ RHS, so the line must pass through the origin. Ed's line does not.
